summary.intent: Plan and execute GSD phase 68.2 (SDK-owned read chain and resolved folder listings) for cipher-box end-to-end: research, scope decisions, pattern mapping, 12-plan/7-wave execution, phase verification, and (after a gap was found) kick off gap-closure planning — while also spinning up an independent worktree for phase 69.
summary.outcome: All 12 original plans executed and committed (62 commits), with the SDK-mediation boundary (D-07) proven GATE_CLEAN and 4/5 must-haves verified, but the phase's headline goal (SC#5 desync fix) was found unmet because `ensureFolderLoaded`/`listFolder` structurally can't re-resolve from cache; a 2-plan gap-closure cycle (68.2-13/14) was planned, plan-checked, and began executing when the transcript ends.

repo: gsd-tools query commit helper has a known false-negative: it can report `commit_failed` even when the commit landed cleanly in git log — always verify with git log before treating it as a real failure.

Requirement checkboxes (e.g. SDK-READ-01/02/04 in REQUIREMENTS.md) must not be marked [x] until the acceptance criteria's deletion step actually lands — multiple wave executors prematurely marked requirements complete before their dependent service deletions (Wave 6/plan 11); this had to be manually reverted and re-marked.

In this pnpm monorepo, worktree-based parallel execution is not worth it when most waves are single-plan: each worktree needs its own `pnpm install` (expensive) and provides no parallelism benefit for single-plan waves — sequential execution on the main tree with git-index care per wave is preferred.

worktree.baseRef defaults can matter: confirming `baseRef: "head"` (not `fresh`/origin-based) before dispatching worktree executors is necessary or they'd fork without in-flight commits (e.g. missing new PLAN.md files).

Planner coverage gaps are a real risk in wide refactors: components/files that merely *consume* a data type being migrated (e.g. SealedChildRef→ResolvedChild) can be left unowned by any plan and only surface when an executor greps for remaining importers before a deletion step.
grep glob syntax intended for other shells can silently choke under zsh — reissue with zsh-safe quoting/globbing rather than trusting an empty/garbled result.

ScheduleWakeup delay calculations must be based on a freshly-fetched current time, not a timestamp computed before a quota interruption — a stale-timestamp delay caused a ~25min miss on a requested wake time.

code.finding: ensureFolderLoaded short-circuits on cached folderTree entries and never re-resolves the folder's IPNS on repeat navigation — root cause of the SC#5 desync bug (owner can't see grantee's shared-folder upload without writing first).
Plan 01 added the ROT-07 enforceResolved gate to the root resolve site on the SDK-internal read path.
Plan 01 added the ROT-07 enforceResolved gate inside dfsFindFolder's child loop, closing the read-path zero-gating gap.

resolveChildren docstring documents that per-child resolve/unseal failures are skipped (availability tradeoff) safely because the target folder is already gated by Plan-01's ensureFolderLoaded/dfsFindFolder before this runs — an unverifiable sibling is never rendered with stale/attacker content.

workflow: For security-critical or security-adjacent plan waves, independently re-run the acceptance/gate tests rather than trusting the executor's self-reported summary — this caught nothing wrong here but is the discipline that would catch a regressed guarantee.

Before a destructive/consolidating plan (e.g. deleting orphaned services + running an allowlist-free grep gate), run a comprehensive pre-flight residual-importer audit — the planner's estimate of affected files can undercount by ~2x (5 flagged vs ~15+ actual importers, 8 needing migration, plus a 9th found mid-execution).
When pausing an in-flight sequential executor for a scheduled resume, let the current plan finish and commit atomically rather than killing it, to avoid a half-committed working tree.

friction: gsd-tools commit helper's `commit_failed` false-negative required repeated manual `git log` verification across multiple commits in this session.
gap-analysis.plan-post parser choked on control characters in the `rendered` field, requiring a direct re-run of the underlying check.
grep glob syntax written for the wrong shell failed silently under zsh during the deletion-blocking importer mapping, requiring a redo.
git fetch failed from the sandboxed session (no network access), limiting worktree base verification to the last-known local origin/main ref.
Session hit its usage/quota limit mid-pause; the first ScheduleWakeup call used a stale pre-quota-gap timestamp and would have resumed 25 minutes late, requiring a manual recompute and reschedule.
A stray/orphaned ScheduleWakeup could not be cleanly retracted after the user said to skip the wait, requiring a workaround (treat its eventual firing as a no-op).

Wave 4 executors (plans 01, 03, 05) repeatedly and incorrectly marked SDK-READ requirement checkboxes complete before their deletion-dependent acceptance criteria were actually satisfied, requiring manual correction.
